2.text: the ermine, known as a guardian spirit, can transform itself, if need be,

3.text: into a polar bear, has something to do with this belief.

4.text: A “giant thunder-bird” is sometimes regarded as the same as the super-

5.text: natural Raven; but more frequently it is a kind of “giant eagle” of super-

6.text: natural strength. In one tale a female “giant eagle” appears as mistress of

7.text: good and bad weather. When visited in her own world by two mortals, she

8.text: undertakes, at their request, to clear the sky, and begins to scrape it with a

9.text: large brass scraper. Noticing that one of the visitors looks at her naked

10.text: legs, she grows angry, and hurls them both back into our world. Even now

11.text: the eagle is protected by a taboo, and the killing of one is supposed to

12.text: bring on bad weather and famine.

13.text: The Asiatic Eskimo also say that the thunder-bird is a “giant eagle.” After the death of

14.text: such an eagle, Upper Being takes his heart, which is immortal, and suspends it on a thread from

15.text: the sky. The suspended heart beats on, producing thunder. After a while the eagle revives. Ac-

16.text: cording to Koryak beliefs, the souls of deceased persons are suspended on cords, in the house of

17.text: the Upper Being, till their return to earth for a new life.¹
17.note: Footnote marker superscript U+00B9, tight against the period. mz draft had it as an ASCII '!'.

20.text: he can stretch his long neck so as to swallow easily a whale-boat, which will

29.text: country it means a “giant fish”² which lives in some inland lakes. It is a

30.text: man-eater, and occasionally takes people while bathing and devours them. Once

31.text: it caught a young man who came to the shore to catch fish. His father,

32.text: seeking revenge, loaded four sledges with deer-meat, tied them together,

33.text: securing them with a very strong double-twisted hide cable, and sank them

34.text: to the bottom of the lake. The fish bit into the bait; but its teeth became

35.text: wedged among the broken ribs of the sledges, and it might have been hauled

36.text: in by the united force of several men.
